name: prev_day_hl_reversal_5s
author: adapted from Gemini Quant
thesis: Exploits 'liquidity hunting' at major pivots. The Previous Day High (PDH) and Low (PDL) are significant levels where retail traders place stop orders. Price often 'tags' these levels, executes the stops (liquidity grab), and then reverses. Institutional algos fade these moves once liquidity is tapped.
mechanism: Previous day's high/low are key reference levels where stop-losses and pending orders cluster. When price approaches these levels, two forces compete: breakout orders above/below and reversal traders fading the move. The resolution depends on volume — high-volume breaches trigger cascading stops, while low-volume approaches tend to reverse.
weaknesses: Breakouts can turn into strong trends
Level 'piercing' can be deep, hitting the stop loss first
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
